source.original_text: The reciprocal cosine spectrum has an absolutely and uniformly convergent cosine expansion. \lambda(\theta)^{-1}=\frac1{\sqrt\kappa}\left(1+2\sum_{j\ge1}(-r)^j\cos(j\theta)\right). Fix \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\) with \(\kappa\ge2\), and set \(r=(\sqrt\kappa-1)/(\sqrt\kappa+1)\). The square root is the nonnegative real square root. For every real angle \(\theta\), define \(\lambda(\theta)=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta/2\). The displayed equality is therefore exactly the source left side \(2/(\kappa+1+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta)\). The source series starts at \(j=1\). Lean uses \(j\in\mathbb N\) and mode \(j+1\) in both the power and cosine. Its partial sum indexed by \(N\) has exactly the first \(N\) positive modes. Absolute convergence is pointwise for each real angle. Uniform convergence is on all \(\mathbb R\) in the angle for this fixed \(\kappa\): one threshold works for every angle. No uniformity over unbounded \(\kappa\) is asserted. The bounds \(0<r<1\), nonzero denominators, summability and uniform convergence are proved internally. No dimension, Gaussian law, matrix input, radius certificate or convergence premise is supplied by the caller.

      (1 / Real.sqrt κ) *
        (1 + 2 * ∑' j : ℕ, (-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ))) ∧
  (∀ θ : ℝ,
    Summable (fun j : ℕ => ‖(-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ)‖)) ∧
  TendstoUniformly
    (fun N : ℕ => fun θ : ℝ =>
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, (-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ))
    (fun θ : ℝ => ∑' j : ℕ, (-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ))
    atTop
decoder_context: Real.sqrt is the nonnegative real square root. All real divisions, norms, powers and cosines have their standard meanings.
The infinite sum over natural j uses exactly the displayed j+1 mode. Finset.range N consists of zero through N minus one, so its partial sum contains the first N positive modes.

Summable of the real norm means absolute convergence of the scalar series. The infinite sum is totalized by convention outside summability, but summability is a conclusion of this proposition, not a caller premise.

TendstoUniformly F f atTop over the real angle means: for every real epsilon>0 there exists a natural N0 such that every N>=N0 and every real angle have absolute F(N,angle)-f(angle)<epsilon. The real parameter is outside this uniformity statement.

reconstruction.text:
# Independent reconstruction of the anonymous statement

For every real number \(\kappa\) satisfying \(2\leq\kappa\), fix
\[
r=r(\kappa):=\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1},
\]
where \(\sqrt{\kappa}\) is the nonnegative real square root. For \(j\in\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\) and \(\theta\in\mathbb R\), write
\[
a_j(\theta):=(-r)^{j+1}\cos\bigl((j+1)\theta\bigr),\qquad
S(\theta):=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}a_j(\theta),\qquad
S_N(\theta):=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}a_j(\theta)\quad(N\in\mathbb N).
\]
The sum defining \(S_0\) is empty and equals zero. All three assertions below hold for this same fixed \(\kappa\) and its associated \(r\):

1. For every real angle \(\theta\),
   \[
   \frac{2}{\kappa+1+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta}
   =\frac{1}{\sqrt{\kappa}}\left(1+2\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}(-r)^{j+1}\cos\bigl((j+1)\theta\bigr)\right).
   \]
2. For every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\), the scalar series is absolutely convergent:
   \[
   \sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\left|(-r)^{j+1}\cos\bigl((j+1)\theta\bigr)\right|<\infty.
   \]
   Equivalently, the displayed sequence of real absolute values is summable.
3. The partial sums \(S_N\) converge uniformly to \(S\) on the entire real angle domain as the natural number \(N\) tends to infinity. Explicitly,
   \[
   \forall\varepsilon\in\mathbb R,\quad
   \varepsilon>0\Longrightarrow
   \exists N_0\in\mathbb N\;\forall N\in\mathbb N,\quad
   N\geq N_0\Longrightarrow
   \forall\theta\in\mathbb R,\quad
   \left|
   \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-r)^{j+1}\cos\bigl((j+1)\theta\bigr)
   -\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}(-r)^{j+1}\cos\bigl((j+1)\theta\bigr)
   \right|<\varepsilon.
   \]

The quantifier order is: choose any real \(\kappa\geq2\), define \(r\) from that \(\kappa\), and assert the conjunction of the two pointwise universally quantified claims and the uniform-convergence claim. In the last claim, \(\varepsilon\) is chosen after \(\kappa\) is fixed, then \(N_0\) is chosen before \(N\) and \(\theta\). Thus \(N_0\) may depend on \(\kappa\) and \(\varepsilon\), but must work for every real \(\theta\) and every natural \(N\geq N_0\). No uniformity as \(\kappa\) varies, explicit convergence rate, or explicit formula for \(N_0\) is asserted.

The only hypothesis on the original mathematical parameter is \(2\leq\kappa\). Summability is a conclusion, not an assumption supplied by a caller. There is no restriction on the real angle. The real norm in the anonymous statement is exactly absolute value. The series starts at \(j=0\), whose term has exponent and frequency \(j+1=1\); the \(N\)-term partial sum therefore contains the positive modes \(1,\ldots,N\). The uniform limit concerns the unscaled series \(S_N\) and \(S\), exactly as displayed above. All numeric constants are the fixed numbers \(0,1,2\); \(r\) is determined by \(\kappa\), not chosen independently. The infinite sum has the usual Lean totalized interpretation outside summability, while the second conclusion establishes summability at every angle here.

No material ambiguity remains after applying the supplied minimal standard-definition context. This is a decoding of the anonymous statement only; no mathematical proof, source comparison, or independent compilation check was performed.

private theorem radius_bounds {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ) :
    1 < Real.sqrt κ ∧
    0 < (Real.sqrt κ - 1) / (Real.sqrt κ + 1) ∧
    (Real.sqrt κ - 1) / (Real.sqrt κ + 1) < 1 := by
  have hsq : (Real.sqrt κ) ^ 2 = κ := Real.sq_sqrt (by linarith)
  have hs : 1 < Real.sqrt κ := by nlinarith [Real.sqrt_nonneg κ]
  have hp : 0 < Real.sqrt κ + 1 := by linarith
  exact ⟨hs, div_pos (by linarith) hp, (div_lt_one hp).2 (by linarith)⟩

private theorem cosine_series_value {r : ℝ} (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr1 : r < 1) (θ : ℝ) :
    1 + 2 * (∑' j : ℕ, (-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ)) =
      (1 - r ^ 2) / (1 + 2 * r * Real.cos θ + r ^ 2) := by
  let z : ℂ := (-r : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((θ : ℂ) * Complex.I)
  have hz : ‖z‖ < 1 := by
    simpa [z, norm_mul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg hr0] using hr1
  have hterm (j : ℕ) : (z ^ j).re = (-r) ^ j * Real.cos ((j : ℝ) * θ) := by
    dsimp [z]
    have hp : (-r : ℂ) ^ j = (((-r) ^ j : ℝ) : ℂ) := by push_cast; rfl
    have he : Complex.exp ((θ : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^ j =
        Complex.exp ((((j : ℝ) * θ : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
      rw [← Complex.exp_nat_mul]
      congr 1
      push_cast
      ring
    rw [mul_pow, hp, he]
    simp only [Complex.mul_re, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, zero_mul,
      sub_zero, Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_re]
  have hreal : HasSum (fun j : ℕ => (-r) ^ j * Real.cos ((j : ℝ) * θ))
      ((1 - z)⁻¹).re := by
    simpa only [hterm] using Complex.hasSum_re (hasSum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one hz)
  have hre : z.re = -r * Real.cos θ := by simp [z, Complex.mul_re]
  have him : z.im = -r * Real.sin θ := by simp [z, Complex.mul_im]
  have hnorm : Complex.normSq (1 - z) = 1 + 2 * r * Real.cos θ + r ^ 2 := by
    rw [Complex.normSq_apply]
    simp only [Complex.sub_re, Complex.one_re, Complex.sub_im, Complex.one_im, hre, him]
    have ht := congrArg (fun x : ℝ => r ^ 2 * x) (Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq θ)
    nlinarith
  have hD : 0 < 1 + 2 * r * Real.cos θ + r ^ 2 := by
    have hm : 0 ≤ r * (1 + Real.cos θ) :=
      mul_nonneg hr0 (by linarith [Real.neg_one_le_cos θ])
    have hp : 0 < (1 - r) ^ 2 := sq_pos_of_pos (by linarith)
    nlinarith
  have hinv : ((1 - z)⁻¹).re =
      (1 + r * Real.cos θ) / (1 + 2 * r * Real.cos θ + r ^ 2) := by
    rw [Complex.inv_re, hnorm]
    simp [hre]
  have hsplit :
      1 + (∑' j : ℕ, (-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ)) =
        (1 + r * Real.cos θ) / (1 + 2 * r * Real.cos θ + r ^ 2) := by
    rw [← hinv, ← hreal.tsum_eq]
    simpa using hreal.summable.tsum_eq_zero_add.symm
  apply (eq_div_iff (ne_of_gt hD)).2
  have hmul := (eq_div_iff (ne_of_gt hD)).1 hsplit
  calc
    _ = 2 * ((1 + (∑' j : ℕ, (-r) ^ (j + 1) *
        Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ))) *
        (1 + 2 * r * Real.cos θ + r ^ 2)) -
        (1 + 2 * r * Real.cos θ + r ^ 2) := by ring
    _ = 1 - r ^ 2 := by rw [hmul]; ring

theorem actual_inverse_spectrum_cosine_expansion {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ) :
  let r : ℝ := (Real.sqrt κ - 1) / (Real.sqrt κ + 1)
  (∀ θ : ℝ,
    2 / (κ + 1 + (κ - 1) * Real.cos θ) =
      (1 / Real.sqrt κ) *
        (1 + 2 * ∑' j : ℕ, (-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ))) ∧
  (∀ θ : ℝ,
    Summable (fun j : ℕ => ‖(-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ)‖)) ∧
  TendstoUniformly
    (fun N : ℕ => fun θ : ℝ =>
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, (-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ))
    (fun θ : ℝ => ∑' j : ℕ, (-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ))
    atTop := by
  dsimp only
  set r : ℝ := (Real.sqrt κ - 1) / (Real.sqrt κ + 1) with hrdef
  obtain ⟨hs1, hr0, hr1⟩ := radius_bounds hκ
  change 0 < r at hr0
  change r < 1 at hr1
  have hgeom : Summable (fun j : ℕ => r ^ (j + 1)) :=
    (summable_nat_add_iff 1).2 (summable_geometric_of_lt_one hr0.le hr1)
  have hmajor (j : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) :
      ‖(-r) ^ (j + 1) * Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ)‖ ≤ r ^ (j + 1) := by
    have hc : |Real.cos (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ)| ≤ 1 :=
      abs_le.mpr ⟨Real.neg_one_le_cos _, Real.cos_le_one _⟩
    simpa [norm_mul, norm_pow, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg hr0.le] using
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hc (pow_nonneg hr0.le (j + 1))
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, tendstoUniformly_tsum_nat hgeom hmajor⟩
  · intro θ
    rw [cosine_series_value hr0.le hr1 θ]
    let s : ℝ := Real.sqrt κ
    have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := by dsimp [s]; linarith
    have hsden : s + 1 ≠ 0 := by dsimp [s]; linarith
    have hs2 : s ^ 2 = κ := Real.sq_sqrt (by linarith)
    have hrdef' : r = (s - 1) / (s + 1) := hrdef
    have hspec : 0 < κ + 1 + (κ - 1) * Real.cos θ := by
      have hm : 0 ≤ (κ - 1) * (1 + Real.cos θ) :=
        mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith [Real.neg_one_le_cos θ])
      linarith
    have hparam : 1 + 2 * r * Real.cos θ + r ^ 2 =
        (1 - r) ^ 2 * (κ + 1 + (κ - 1) * Real.cos θ) / 2 := by
      rw [hrdef', ← hs2]
      field_simp [hsden]
      ring
    have hnorm : 1 - r ^ 2 = s * (1 - r) ^ 2 := by
      rw [hrdef']
      field_simp [hsden]
      ring
    have h1r : 1 - r ≠ 0 := by linarith
    change 2 / (κ + 1 + (κ - 1) * Real.cos θ) =
      (1 / s) * ((1 - r ^ 2) / (1 + 2 * r * Real.cos θ + r ^ 2))
    rw [hnorm, hparam]
    field_simp [hs0, hsden, ne_of_gt hspec, h1r]
  · intro θ
    exact hgeom.of_norm_bounded (fun j => by simpa only [norm_norm] using hmajor j θ)

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumCosineExpansion

steps.title: Produce the geometric radius
steps.text: The source condition gives a square root strictly greater than one. Its literal fractional transform lies strictly between zero and one, so the complex geometric ratios have norm below one.
steps.lean: The private radius_bounds proof uses Real.sq_sqrt and Real.sqrt_nonneg, then positive-denominator division. These are internal outputs, not public hypotheses.

steps.title: Take the real part of a convergent geometric series
steps.text: Set z=−r exp(iθ). The complex phase has modulus one. Sum the geometric series and take its real part; De Moivre identifies each real term with the cosine mode. This packages the source pair of conjugate geometric sums by real-part linearity.
steps.lean: cosine_series_value invokes hasSum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one and Complex.hasSum_re. hterm checks the casts and exp_nat_mul identity explicitly; hreal carries an actual HasSum certificate.

steps.title: Compute the real rational expression
steps.text: The squared norm of 1−z is the positive denominator D. The real part of its inverse is (1+r cosθ)/D. Separate the zero mode, then double the positive modes and subtract the zero term.
steps.lean: hre, him and hnorm use the trigonometric unit-circle identity; hD is produced from r<1 and cosθ≥−1. Complex.inv_re and hreal.summable.tsum_eq_zero_add give hsplit; the final calculation proves the displayed rational identity.

steps.title: Restore the exact source normalization
steps.text: Substitute the literal radius and s²=κ. Two algebraic identities cancel the positive factors and yield the reciprocal source eigenvalue, with the exact factor two and square-root scale.
steps.lean: hparam and hnorm in the public producer prove these identities by field algebra; hspec and h1r supply nonzero denominators internally. The sealed pointwise conclusion follows from cosine_series_value.

steps.title: Prove absolute and uniform convergence
steps.text: Every absolute mode is bounded by the same positive geometric mode. The geometric majorant is summable. It proves absolute summability at each angle and, through the uniform majorant test, convergence of the partial sums uniformly over every real angle.
steps.lean: hgeom proves the shifted geometric sum is summable. hmajor uses the real cosine bound. Summable.of_norm_bounded yields the absolute output, and tendstoUniformly_tsum_nat yields exactly the sealed all-real-angle uniform output.

steps.title: Consume the expansion on the actual finite grid
steps.text: For d≥2 and the literal hard grid, the private Test takes cosine weights at any natural frequency n. It consumes the new pointwise expansion and absolute summability, proves weighted summability, normalizes each reciprocal eigenvalue and genuinely exchanges the finite grid sum with the infinite series. This is a private generalized intermediate, before Gaussian expectation identification or alias cancellation.
steps.lean: actual_inverse_grid_cosine_series obtains heq and habs from the new canonical producer. hs, hsg and hlin use absolute summability; heigen proves literal reciprocal normalization; Summable.tsum_finsetSum is the actual exchange. The compiled private proof has exactly one public ASTIS parent, this producer; it is not a Registry node or a C8 Gaussian moment theorem.
